scope: Bounded review of selected framing, aggregate, and introductory clauses around graphics, XObjects, images, and transparency. The individual obligations owned by child audits are cross-referenced, not recertified. No new tests were run or production/ledger files edited.
source_method: Read the effective sponsored EC3 PDF and checked printed-page footers. Printed page numbers below are paired with the physical PDF page. No applicable annotation or erratum was found for the specific aggregate text unless stated; the known transparency annotations #345 and #688 are recorded below.

features.source: §8.4.1, physical 171–174 / printed 156–159, including Tables 51–52. It has a reader SHALL to maintain and initialize graphics state. Beyond the initial-value tables, its general rules require parameter values to have proper types/ranges, numeric values to be clipped when needed, and prohibit storing device-capability adjustment back into state. §8.4.3 is an introduction to parameter detail; it adds no independent behavior.
features.ledger_and_code: doc/conformance/ledger.toml rows 8.4–8.4.3 call the parent implemented and cite selected line-parameter tests. GraphicsState::initial and Stroke::default realize initial values; state setters and paint-time device-width calculation separate clipping from device adjustment. `coordinates_graphics_state_current` reviewed selected defaults and q/Q, and `scan_conversion_current` separately owns relevant scan-conversion parameters.
features.assertions: line_parameters.rs directly checks several Table 51 defaults, negative line-width and sub-one miter clipping, and that the one-device-pixel stroke adjustment happens at paint time rather than being stored. This is selected evidence, not a full assertion of every field in Tables 51–52 or every parameter setter.
features.assessment: No new behavior defect identified. The aggregate ledger note is materially broader than the cited test list, but existing child reviews supply more evidence; the evidence is distributed and does not establish every parameter's initialization, range clamp, and no-device-adjust-back behavior. Treat the parent status as an aggregate routing claim, not proof from its one cited test.

features.source: §8.5 family introduction is physical 184 / printed 169; §8.5.2 operator rules are physical 185–186 / printed 170–171; §8.5.3 is physical 187–190 / printed 172–175, including .3.3 Filling at physical 189–190 / printed 174–175. The family introduction says path construction defines geometry and path painting ends the path; .2/.3 have the operator-specific requirements, and .3.3 defines nonzero/even-odd fill rules.
features.ledger_and_code: The ledger points to graphics/path operators and `stroke_fill_geometry_current` plus earlier `path_painting` assertions. Existing audits own fill rules, clipping/path termination and stroke/fill geometry. This frame pass did not rerun those assertions.
features.assessment: No new independent requirement was found in the aggregate headings. No new test draft: a broad family-level duplicate would add little beyond the existing discriminating path controls.

features.source: §8.7.1, physical 234–235 / printed 219–220, introduces tiling and shading patterns and their color-position/stream descriptions; the substantive syntax, matrices, cell clipping, BBoxes and shading types belong to §§8.7.2–.4.5. No family heading licenses omission of a child requirement.
features.ledger_and_code: `pattern_forms_current` reviewed pattern spaces, tiling-cell state, types, transform and BBox interactions; `shading_type1_current` and `shading_current` own shading geometry/types. The confirmed degenerate tiling BBox issue and pending unexecuted draft are in the former shard; the Type 1 shading draft is parent-promoted. This pass adds no duplicate test.
features.assessment: No separate aggregate-level rule missed. The recorded child findings remain the operative evidence; no claim is made here that every pattern or shading subtype is certified.

features.source: §8.8.1 begins at physical 268 / printed 253; Table 86 is physical 269 / printed 254 and specifies Do resource lookup, stream Type-if-present, and Image/Form dispatch. §8.9.2–.3 requires image format/data/coordinate/color mapping to be specified and describes sample packing. §8.9.5.1 contains the image-dictionary row requirements; §8.9.6.1 introduces masking mechanisms and defers their behavior to the specialized clauses.
features.ledger_and_code: `content/run/xobject_ops.rs` routes Do to `draw_xobject`; `content/xobject.rs` resolves the current XObject resource, requires a stream, then dispatches image/form. `images_samples_interpolation_current`, `image_filters_remaining_current`, image-mask shards, and `transparency_foundations_current` own their respective semantics. The prior `images_current` finding about malformed Decode component handling is the concrete §8.9.5.1 reader-error concern; it is not re-established by this frame review.
features.assessment: No new XObject dispatch mismatch identified in this bounded review. A successful valid-XObject consumer test is available in the form/image child suites. This pass does not turn malformed dictionary recovery into a valid-input defect and does not recertify all image filters or mask precedence.

features.source: §8.10.3 and Table 94, physical 289–290 / printed 274–275: a group is a form XObject with an optional Group attributes entry; every group dictionary has required `/S`; `/Type` is optional and, if present, shall be `/Group`. The Type sentence is a well-formedness/producerside constraint, distinct from a reader command to reject or fail to render when Type is absent or wrong.
features.ledger_and_code: Table 94 feature `group_type_if_present` is marked unreviewed in the current round inventory. `form_xobjects_audit.rs` exercises Form invocation; `transparency_groups.rs` and group-construction tests exercise actual `/S /Transparency` group behavior. Reader dispatch checks the Group dictionary's `/S`, but does not gate rendering on the optional `/Type` tag.
features.assessment: Do not classify the missing `/Type` reader gate as a conformance defect from this source sentence alone. The implementation/test map should state that this Table 94 key is not consumed, and its producer-validity nature should be explicit. No reader-side test draft is warranted. The broad group behavior remains owned by §11.4 and §11.6.6 audits.

features.source: §11.1, physical 402 / printed 387, says equivalent results may be obtained without copying the specification's implementation-like descriptions. §11.2, physical 402–404 / printed 387–389, defines the bottom-to-top transparency stack; result at a point is determined by all enclosing objects, blend mode, shape and opacity; compositing results become the next backdrop. Note 1 expressly says processors need not paint/rasterize in source order or commit to intermediate raster output. These are substantive model requirements, while Figure 71 is illustrative.
features.ledger_and_code: Prior child shards cover the compositing formula, group recurrence/isolated and knockout behavior, masks, blend modes, and actual CPU consumer. CPU group rendering uses buffers and a single group blit; different optimized paths are reviewed against their stated premises in `transparency_compositing_current` and `transparency_groups_current`.
features.assessment: The implementation's deferred/group-buffer approach is permitted by Note 1; painting-order tests need observable stack results rather than identical intermediate rasters. No new independent test or defect found in the framing prose.

features.source: These aggregate headings organize the computation, group, mask, PDF-encoding and rendering clauses; they do not certify the child formulas by themselves. §11.6.2 has the elementary-object rule that one graphics object is one transparency element; no part of one object composites with another part of itself. §11.7.1, physical 440 / printed 425, is only a sentence introducing interactions with colour specification/rendering and has no independent SHALL.
features.ledger_and_code: Relevant owner audits: `transparency_foundations_current` (§11.3.1–.2, 11.4.1–.3, 11.5.1–.2, 11.6.1); `transparency_compositing_current` (§11.3.3–.8, 11.4.4/.5/.7/.8, 11.6.4.4); `transparency_groups_current` (group result and consumers); `stroke_composition_consumers_current` (single-object overlap, B39); `pattern_forms_current`/`shading_type1_current` (pattern and shading geometry); `rendering_intent_transfer_current`, `default_colour_bpc_current`, and `overprint_transparency_current` (§11.7 slices). These audits report bounded cases, not whole-clause proof.
features.errata: EC3 #345 on physical 407–408 / printed 392–393 labels Figures 72–73 as illustrative rather than pixel/color precise; no numeric oracle here relies on the figures. #688 on physical 428 / printed 413 corrects two alpha symbols in the §11.4.8 summary. It does not amend the §11.4.2 recurrence reviewed in `transparency_foundations_current`. The separate #619 carets on physical 436 concern Table 143 / §11.6.5.2 entries and should not be filed as a change to §11.6.6.
features.assessment: No new aggregate-level mismatch found. The notable valid-input consumer failure remains the prior B39 single-object alpha-stroke case (CPU expected 128 vs observed 64; direct raster controls and parent review are in `stroke_composition_consumers_current`). This pass does not enlarge its scope or treat an unrun backend draft as evidence.
